Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the CloudForge Q2 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. Please be advised that today's call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, Operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to CloudForge's Q2 FY2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Alex Rivera, CEO; Jordan Lee, CFO; Taylor Kim, CTO; Morgan Patel, Chief Revenue Officer; and Riley Chen, Chief Product Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements. Actual results may differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm pleased to report on CloudForge's performance for Q2 FY2024. We achieved significant milestones this quarter, driven by strong demand for our ForgeAI Pro and continued execution of our strategic initiatives.

Our focus this quarter was on six key areas: new customer acquisition, cost of revenue breakdown, churn analysis, capital allocation, CAC trends, and NRR performance.

These areas underscore our robust momentum across customer growth, operational efficiency, retention, and strategic investments. For instance, we added a substantial number of new customers, contributing meaningfully to our ARR and MRR, while maintaining tight control over costs and driving expansions that offset any churn.

To dive deeper into these and the financials, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee to discuss in more detail.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $250 million, representing a 28% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin was 68.7%, and operating income was $45 million.

Let me start with new customer acquisition, which remains a core driver of our top-line growth in this competitive SaaS landscape. In Q2, we added 1,450 net new customers, marking a robust 28% year-over-year increase from the 1,130 added in Q2 FY2023. This brings our total customer count to 18,200 as of quarter-end, up 22% YoY.

Our new logo additions contributed $18.2 million in new ARR during the quarter—a 32% YoY uplift from the $13.8 million in Q2 last year. On an MRR basis, this equated to $1.52 million in incremental monthly recurring revenue. These figures reflect an average annual contract value of approximately $62,000 across new customers, skewed higher by our enterprise wins, where the median ACV exceeded $250,000.

Breaking this down by segment, our go-to-market strategy continues to balance self-serve scalability with high-value enterprise motion. In enterprise, with ACV over $100K, we landed 42 new logos, up 50% YoY, including several multi-year deals with household names in fintech and healthcare. These contributed $14.5 million, or 80% of our new ARR, with strong land-and-expand potential evidenced by our 135% dollar-based net expansion rate in the cohort.

Mid-market, ACV $25K to $100K, saw 210 new customers, a 35% YoY increase, fueled by our partner ecosystem with integrators like AWS Marketplace and Microsoft AppSource, adding $3.1 million in new ARR.

SMB and self-serve, ACV under $25K, delivered the bulk at 1,198 net adds, up 25% YoY, driven by freemium-to-paid conversions. While lower ACV at around $4,500, this high-volume channel delivered $600K in new ARR and boasts our best payback period at under 8 months on CAC.

Regionally, North America remained our powerhouse, accounting for 68% of new adds with 980 customers and $12.4M new ARR, bolstered by our San Francisco HQ proximity to tech hubs and a maturing sales org. EMEA saw explosive 45% YoY growth with 320 new customers and $3.8M ARR, thanks to GDPR-compliant AI features that resonated post our London data center launch. APAC contributed 150 adds and $2.0M ARR, up 30% YoY, with early traction in Japan via partnerships, though macro headwinds like yen volatility tempered deal sizes.

What underpinned this? Product-led growth enhancements from our Q1 revamp of self-serve onboarding reduced time-to-value from 14 days to 4 days, lifting conversion rates by 22%, with AI-driven product tours driving 40% of SMB wins. The launch of ForgeAI Pro closed 25% of enterprise deals as a key expansion driver, with early adopters seeing 3x usage uplift. Sales efficiency kept CAC steady at $28K enterprise-wide, down 5% QoQ, with LTV/CAC at 5.2x thanks to refined intent data from 6sense integrations and 1.8x quota attainment in inside sales. Partner momentum via Salesforce AppExchange and Google Cloud Marketplace represented 18% of new ARR, accelerating ramp times by 30%.

New customer cohorts are expanding faster than ever—our Q2 vintage already at 118% NRR within 90 days, well above the 110-115% SaaS industry benchmark. Churn remains elite at 4.2% gross dollar churn. We're doubling down on verticalization—healthcare and fintech now 35% of pipeline—while navigating elongated sales cycles up 10% to 95 days enterprise. For Q3, we guide to 1,600-1,800 net new customers and $20M-$22M new ARR, assuming stable macro conditions. Our land-and-expand flywheel, combined with R&D investments at 22% of revenue, gives us conviction in outgrowing the SaaS market's projected 18% CAGR through 2027.

Now, turning to our cost of revenue breakdown, which came in at $78.2 million in Q2, representing 31.3% of total revenue—or a robust 68.7% gross margin, up 210 basis points year-over-year. This continues our trajectory of gross margin expansion, now at 68% on a trailing twelve-month basis, ahead of our long-term target of 70-72% as we scale.

Hosting and infrastructure costs accounted for 42% of COR, or $32.8 million—up just 12% year-over-year despite 28% revenue growth. This is driven primarily by public cloud spend on AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud Platform for our multi-tenant SaaS platform. We're running a consumption-based model where customer usage of our AI-powered data pipelines and real-time collaboration features correlates with egress traffic, storage, and compute.

We've seen a 15% sequential decline in cost per active user, thanks to committed use discounts and savings plans covering 65% of our AWS footprint, yielding $12 million in annualized savings. We've also completed 40% of our migration to ARM-based Graviton instances on AWS, delivering 20-30% better price-performance for containerized workloads on Kubernetes. APAC hosting costs ticked up 8% quarter-over-quarter due to surging demand from enterprise customers, but we've offset this by launching sovereign cloud instances in Japan and Singapore to comply with data residency regs.

Strategically, our multi-cloud strategy—45% AWS, 35% Azure, 20% GCP—has improved net reliable capacity by 25% and positioned us for AI workloads, where we're piloting NVIDIA GPU reservations for GenAI features, showing 3x inference speed at 40% lower cost.

Next, personnel-related costs for customer support and success, 28% of COR at $21.9 million—flat year-over-year as a percentage of revenue. This includes 24/7 global support teams, onboarding specialists, and technical account managers driving 95%+ gross retention. We've grown support headcount by only 5% to 450 FTEs, but productivity is up 22% thanks to AI copilots in Zendesk and Intercom automating 60% of L1 tickets.

EMEA support costs are higher at 35% of regional COR due to multilingual requirements and GDPR-driven SLAs under 2 hours. In the Americas, self-serve knowledge bases reduced paid support touches by 18%. We're investing $5 million in Q3 for a new Customer Success Platform to boost NRR from 118% to 122% by identifying expansion opportunities.

Amortization of acquired intangibles and developed technology is 16% of COR, or $12.5 million—steady as we lap the 2022 acquisition of DataSync AI, realizing 150% ROI and accelerating time-to-market for zero-ETL pipelines.

The residual 14%, or $10.9 million, covers third-party data feeds from S&P Global and weather APIs, payment processing fees via Stripe at 0.8% of ARR, and royalties for open-source components like Apache Kafka. We've negotiated volume discounts, shaving 10% off fees YoY.

Overall, COR grew just 14% year-over-year versus 28% revenue growth, delivering 140 basis points of margin expansion, fueled by 25% infrastructure efficiency at $0.12 per compute hour and higher-ARPU enterprise seats at 72% of ARR. Challenges like inflationary cloud pricing and FX headwinds persist, but guidance embeds leverage to 32-33% of revenue in H2. We're targeting sub-30% COR long-term through AI ops reducing idle capacity by 30%, customer-led migrations, and R&D spillovers.

Now, on churn dynamics, which remain a cornerstone of our financial health. Our logo churn came in at 7.2%, a 15% improvement year-over-year from 8.5%, and down from 7.8% in Q1. Dollar-based net revenue retention—or DBNR—was a robust 112%, outperforming the median SaaS benchmark of 105-108%.

By cohort, enterprise customers with $250K+ ARR saw logo churn of just 3.1%, with DBNR at 118%, fueled by multi-year renewals and upsells into SalesPredict. SMBs under $50K ARR ticked up to 11.5% logo churn from 10.8%, pressured by budgets. North America held at 6.8%, EMEA rose to 9.1% due to compliance and currency issues, while APAC improved to 5.9% on mobile-first features.

Root-cause analysis from our Customer Health Score model aggregating 47 signals shows: macroeconomic pressures at 42% of churn, with 28% citing budget reallocations and SMBs downsizing to freemium alternatives; competitive shifts at 25%, with rivals like Pipedrive and Zoho gaining via discounting and AI switches to Gong; onboarding friction at 18%, with low-usage cohorts churning 3x higher; and product/support gaps at 15%, like EMEA GDPR and APAC latency.

Expansion revenue hit $18.7M, up 22% YoY, offsetting $12.4M contraction.

Our Churn Zero initiative has reduced at-risk accounts by 20%: proactive CSMs with AI playbooks and QBRs boosted renewals 14%, health scoring flags issues 60 days early, CSAT to 88 and NPS to 52. Product innovations like GenAI Forecasting drove 35% adoption and $4.2M expansion ARR; usage-based pricing cut SMB churn 18%; 50+ no-code connectors slashed onboarding to 21 days with 92% Day 30 adoption. Regional tailoring includes $5M for EMEA compliance and APAC edge computing. Flexible pay-as-you-grow tiers retained 85% at-risk SMBs, with 42% cross-sell attach rates.

For Q3, expect logo churn below 7% and DBNR to 114%, with $2.1B ARR and $150M RPO up 28% YoY. Goal: sub-5% enterprise churn and 110%+ DBNR by FY25 end.

Turning to capital allocation, which remains a cornerstone of driving long-term shareholder value. We generated $1.2 billion in free cash flow over the past 12 months, ending with $3.8 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments. This gives flexibility across organic investments, strategic acquisitions, share repurchases, and debt management.

Our philosophy prioritizes high-ROI opportunities accelerating Rule of 40 metrics, targeting 25-30%+ ARR growth and margins over 30%, vetted through a 20% IRR hurdle.

Organic investments: R&D at 28% of revenue, $320 million in Q2, focused on Nexus AI Suite for agentic AI in B2B verticals, showing 35% productivity uplift and 22% churn reduction. 15% of R&D, $50 million, to APAC localization and sovereign cloud; $80 million to cybersecurity with zero-trust and ML anomaly detection. NRR hit 118%, dollar net expansion 125%.

Strategic acquisitions: $450 million YTD across three tuck-ins. $320 million for DataForge Analytics added real-time data lakes, cross-sold to 60 accounts for $12 million Q4 ARR and 300 bps margin expansion. $85 million for EuroComply regtech and $45 million for AIForge Labs vertical LLMs. $1 billion dry powder for cybersecurity and verticals at 8x forward ARR.

Share repurchases: $280 million in Q2 at $145 average, retiring 2.1 million shares; YTD $650 million, $1.5 billion authorized. Shares undervalued at 7.5x forward FCF.

Debt: Repurchased $300 million convertibles at 15% discount; net debt/EBITDA 0.8x.

Forward: $800 million to $1.2 billion next 12 months—50% R&D, 30% M&A, 15% buybacks, 5% bolt-ons.

On CAC trends, our blended CAC was $428 in Q2, a 12% sequential improvement from $486 and 18% YoY decline from $522. This brings LTV:CAC to 4.8x and payback to 14 months.

By segment: SMB $295, flat seq but down 22% YoY on PLG with 68% self-serve ARR; mid-market $1,240, down 15% seq/25% YoY on SEO and partnerships cutting cycles 22%; enterprise $11,750, down 8% seq/14% YoY on ABM and 42% upsell.

Regionally: North America $410 down 20% YoY; EMEA $520 with London pod trimming 10%; APAC $610 accelerating with partners.

Flywheel: PLG top-funnel, ABM enterprise, AI sales cockpit up close rates 19%. Q3 guide $410-$420, LTV:CAC 5.0x+.

Finally, NRR at 118%, 8th quarter above 115%, up 600 bps YoY, top quartile vs. peers.

Expansion 22 points from seat additions, AI ForgeAI Predict, consumption pricing; contraction 1.5 points via workshops; churn 2.5% logo/3.8% dollar, gross retention 96%. North America 120%, EMEA 116%, APAC 110%.

Platform flywheel with 420 new logos, 42% expanding. Targeting 120%+ FY25.

We continue to invest in research and development to drive innovation and expand our product offerings. Our cash position remains strong, providing flexibility for strategic acquisitions and growth. We are updating our full-year guidance to $1.02 billion to $1.05 billion in revenue.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Taylor Kim for a technology update.

Taylor Kim:
Thank you, Jordan. This quarter, we made significant progress in advancing our AI capabilities and further integrating them into our core platform. We are seeing strong adoption of our new AI-powered features, which are driving increased user engagement and improved customer outcomes. We've also focused on enhancing our platform's security and scalability to meet the growing demands of our enterprise customers.

And now Riley Chen will provide an update on the product roadmap.

Riley Chen:
Thank you, Taylor. We have been focusing on the user experience of our products and are excited to announce the launch of AI-powered workflow automation suite. This new feature significantly improves productivity and customization. We are seeing strong adoption of this feature which aligns with our product strategy.

Now, I'll turn the call back to the operator for Q&A.

Operator:
Thank you. To ask a question, press star then one. Our first question comes from Ben Smith with Goldman Sachs.

Ben Smith:
Hi, good afternoon. Can you discuss the impact of ForgeAI Pro on your overall growth, what kind of attach rates are you seeing, and how it compares to your initial expectations?

Morgan Patel:
Thanks, Ben. ForgeAI Pro has been a game-changer, closing 25% of our enterprise deals and contributing significantly to the $18.2 million in new ARR from 1,450 net adds. Attach rates are strong at 40-42% on renewals and expansions, driving our 135% DBNER in new cohorts and 118% NRR within 90 days—well ahead of expectations, with 3x usage uplift in early adopters and positioning us against competitors like Adobe Sensei.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Chen:
What are your plans for international expansion, specifically in the APAC region, and what are your key target markets?

Alex Rivera:
Great question, Lisa. International remains a priority, with EMEA up 45% YoY on 320 new customers and $3.8M ARR from GDPR features and London data center, APAC at 30% growth with 150 adds and $2.0M ARR via Japan partnerships. For APAC, we're scaling our Singapore hub, investing in sovereign cloud, edge computing for latency, and localizing for markets like Japan, Australia, India, and Southeast Asia—targeting fintech, healthcare, and manufacturing with 15% of R&D allocated there to tap the $200 billion CRM TAM at 18% CAGR.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Park with JPMorgan.

David Park:
How are you managing churn in the current economic environment, what's the trend you are seeing in NRR, and what are your strategies to improve customer retention?

Jordan Lee:
Thanks, David. Churn is well-managed at 7.2% logo, down 15% YoY, with DBNR at 112% and overall NRR at 118% trending up 600 bps YoY. Macro pressures drive 42% of it, but expansions at 22 points offset. Strategies include Churn Zero with AI health scoring, QBRs upping renewals 14%, GenAI upsells at 35% adoption, usage pricing cutting SMB churn 18%, and regional fixes like EMEA compliance. Expect Q3 logo churn under 7%, NRR to 114%, targeting 120%+ FY25.

Operator:
Thank you. I'm showing no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain committed to delivering strong results for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again on our next earnings call.

Operator:
Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
